    Tech Report: Same old Spurs given reality check of epic proportions

    📅 22 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (5031 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Recent findings suggest that the players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur.
    • Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.
    • But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Recent findings suggest that the players and the transfer fees might be different, but this was same old Tottenham Hotspur. The same Tottenham that finished each of the last two seasons in 17th. The same Tottenham that folded in adversity. The same Tottenham that opposition fans loved to laugh at.

    Of course, it is very early days and the good news for Spurs fans and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is the side that started the opening day humiliation to Brentford may well never play together again this season.

    But in a summer in which Tottenham have allowed their fans to dream of good times ahead by breaking the bank in the transfer window, this was a reality check of epic proportions.

    The Spurs supporters who have become sick of being made the butt of their rivals’ jokes had to listen to Brentford fans singing “Thomas Frank, he’s laughing at you” in reference to the Dane’s unhappy spell in north London.

    The impending arrival of Savinho will take Tottenham’s spending over £300m, but none of their substantial-money debutants at the Gtech Community Stadium hit the ground running.

    There was only one man who looked anything close to a £100m player and it was not Sandro Tonali.

    Tottenham’s first-ever £100m signing was completely upstaged by Brentford’s Mamadou Sangaré on his first competitive start for the club, as Spurs were run ragged.

    Sources indicate that sangaré might not have scored on his Brentford debut, but he had a major contribution in two of his side’s goals and bossed the middle of the park. He deservedly received a standing ovation when he was substituted with 15 minutes remaining.

    “He is a top player, no doubt about it,” mentioned head coach Keith Andrews. “He is the one we were after in the window. The club deserve a lot of credit because a lot of clubs were looking at him.

    “He deserves a lot of credit too, because he could have gone elsewhere for a few more bob. He recognised this would be a good place to come and he has settled quite nicely.”.

    Industry observers note that A club-record £39m signing from French club Lens, Sangaré may prove to be a steal for Brentford. He ran the game for long periods and was responsible for Keane Lewis-Potter’s opening goal.

    Having played a lovely one-two with Dango Ouattara, Sangaré kept his cool to brilliantly pick out Lewis-Potter and give him the easy task of finding the back of the net.

    Keane Lewis-Potter scores Brentford's first goal of the fresh season!Brilliant play from record signing Mamadou Sangaré 👏 pic.twitter.com/Ua9HklQaWh.

    Later in the first half, Sangaré won a free-kick in his own half thanks to some quick feet and the action produced a big cheer from the home fans.

    Sources indicate that tonali was the subject of chants of “what a waste of money” from Brentford supporters. It was a volley that sailed high over the crossbar that prompted that particular song, but Tonali was not just off target with his shooting.

    Sources indicate that he lost possession on a couple of occasions at both ends of the pitch and allowed Brentford players to glide past him during the opening stages of the match. He struggled to get around the pitch and Tottenham generally lacked desire and fight – two things that clubs cannot buy.

    According to recent reports, richarlison, Lucas Bergvall and goalkeeper Antonin Kinsky can all be disappointed with Brentford’s second goal. Richarlison’s hold-up play was terrible, Bergvall produced a weak challenge that allowed Mathias Jensen to take the ball and shoot, and Kinsky parried the ball straight into the path of Vitaly Janelt, who scored.

    Kinsky has been trusted to take over from Guglielmo Vicario as Tottenham’s number one this season, but this was not a good start.

    It has been revealed that vitaly Janelt doubles Brentford's lead! 🐝 pic.twitter.com/AYh5BGhJBQ.

    De Zerbi spent much of the first half telling his back four to get higher up the pitch and it was perhaps understandable that captain for the day Archie Gray, Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi and Andy Robertson looked like a group of strangers.

    This was the foursome’s first competitive game together, but De Zerbi will need his Tottenham players to get to know each other as fast as possible if they are to challenge for Europe this season or even finish in the top half of the table.

    Sources indicate that bergvall and Conor Gallagher were hooked at half-time, with Tottenham two goals behind and De Zerbi clearly unimpressed. But the Italian’s changes did not prompt an instant response. In fact, things got even worse.

    Once again, Sangaré was heavily involved. He produced a well-hit shot that Kinsky had to save. For the second time, the goalkeeper failed to push the ball out of trouble and Michael Kayode was able to score.

    According to recent reports, michael Kayode with a third for Brentford just three minutes into the second half! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/40kOIlV5MU.

    Igor Thiago missed a penalty after substitute Rodrigo Bentancur fouled Kevin Schade, as Spurs threatened to completely collapse with the result already pretty much decided.

    In a recent development, igor Thiago's penalty CRASHES off the post! ❌ pic.twitter.com/jZUEoIA44h.

    Sources indicate that de Zerbi can console himself with the fact his Spurs team will swiftly look a lot different. There are more newly introduced faces to come in, with winger Savinho on the brink of joining and Tottenham hoping Omar Marmoush will follow him from Manchester City.

    Mikey Moore, who forced Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher into two second-half saves, is expected to join Cologne on loan and Mohammed Kudus is close to returning from injury, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro will come back in.

    But if ever there was proof that spending a fortune offers no guarantee of happiness, then this was it.

    Roberto De Zerbi has admitted that big-spending Tottenham Hotspur “are not a team yet” after watching his fresh-look side fall to an opening-day defeat to Brentford.

    Tottenham have splashed out over £200m on fresh players, but head coach De Zerbi has warned it will be impossible to set any targets until they become a team.

    Record £100m signing Sandro Tonali made his competitive debut for Tottenham, along with fellow fresh signings Jan Paul van Hecke, Marcos Senesi, Mateus Fernandes and Andy Robertson.

    Tottenham have been tipped to challenge for European qualification, having finished 17th in each of the last two seasons, but De Zerbi acknowledged those optimistic predictions may have come too soon.

    It has been revealed that his team looked like strangers in their humiliating loss at Brentford and the Italian said: “We are not a team yet for a lot of reasons. We can fix the target [for the season] when you become a team. Before you become a team, you can’t say what you can do.

    Recent findings suggest that “You can’t become a team from the transfer market on paper. You become a team when the players find a connection, a spirit, a soul.

    “We are not at the right point in our physical condition for a lot of reasons. Late from the World Cup and because in Australia [on pre-season], we don’t work in the right way. But no excuses, it’s a normal situation when you are building a upcoming project. I don’t want time but we have to pass through these problems.

    Industry observers note that “I am surprised by the result and performance. They [Brentford] deserved to win and we played very bad. I knew we were not in the right condition. We can’t find an excuse. I am sorry for the result and performance.

    Recent findings suggest that “Marcos Senesi, Jan Paul van Hecke and Sandro Tonali are not in the best physical condition. We knew that before the game. We have to improve on that and many other things, like organisation and pressing.

    “We can improve rapidly but first, we have to understand this game better. I know their physical condition and [they are] new players but we have to put something more.

    “We had to fight more. Players know I have a lot of confidence in them and we hope to improve rapidly. Until we reach these conditions we have to suffer and today is an vital defeat. Maybe we can wake up stronger.”.

    It has been revealed that we had some problems with the timing of the pressure, we arrived too often late. We lost too many duels to compete with Brentford. I am sorry for that and sorry for the defeat. We have to improve in the physical condition and the organisation.

    It has been revealed that it was the first game and part of our journey, we knew we had a lot of new players. To become a team I noted before the game we need two things, soul and style of play. We didn’t fight in the right way. Brentford is maybe one of the most important teams in the Premier League in terms of duels.

    It has been revealed that it was a game, especially in the first half, in one direction. We were not in the right position to make the high pressure, with Mikey Moore on the left centre.

    We didn’t play well, we didn’t play in the right way. I think not because we don’t remember last season, because these players are good people but we lost too many duels. One of the best qualities of Brentford is the one-to-one, the man-to-man and the set-pieces.

    According to recent reports, really pleased. Felt like there was a performance coming, you never really know after pre-season. The reality is the first game of the season comes and it can rapidly come unstuck. I felt good for a number of weeks about how we were coming together. I was pretty pleased.

    Our fans were amazing today. There is a genuine connection here that helps. I thought we started the game brilliantly and they were fully engaged. We want to be relentless. We looked like a real team.

    Sources indicate that that’s what we wanted, we wanted to start sharp, we want to show people what we’re made of and we did that today. We know last season we were one point off, this year, we’ve added quality people to the squad.

    He’s been unbelievable, I can’t praise him high enough. He’s one of them players that we might lose the ball you just know he is going to win it back and he gets us on the counter-attack so swiftly.

    Is that Pedro Porro, Micky Van de Ven and Mohammed Kudus could be back for the next game against Newcastle, and Savinho ought to be through the door.

    Industry observers note that according to Opta, Brentford won the xG battle 3.96 to 0.47, taking 26 shots to Spurs’s nine. De Zerbi’s team finished the game with 59 per cent possession, but that is inflated by Brentford sitting off when three up. It’s the most xG Spurs have conceded in a single game since a 6-3 defeat by Liverpool in December 2024.

    Less Christ the Redeemer more Christ, that was terrible.

    "I think that sums it up"Fair to say this Spurs fan wasn't pleased with their performance 😅 pic.twitter.com/ZAdVaVbjlS.

    Possibly Brentford’s best performance under Keith Andrews, though that may be overstating the strength of the opposition. This was a complete display: they pressed Spurs, they played through Spurs, they played over Spurs, they dominated Spurs from set-pieces and their defenders bullied Spurs’s forwards. It will be interesting to hear from De Zerbi and whether he is philosophical or irate. This is far from Spurs’s ideal projected team, but still unacceptable.

    Sources indicate that kinsky palms away a Damsgaard corner, and Yarmoliuk slices his shot over the bar. We are deep into stoppage time, and Brentford’s players are still pressing Bentnacur and Senesi and making them play with their heads down.

    Sources indicate that just four minutes of added time to play but Spurs have more defending to do in the shape over another Brentford corner. They survive, but Brentford rapidly establish possession again.

    It would appear Lord Sugar is still watching:.

    To all Spurs fans don't worry this is all tactical to lure other teams into believing we are a easy touch. #coys.

    Another Brentford debut: Callum Wilson replaces Igor Thiago. Destiny Udogie has replaced Archie Gray for Spurs. “You should have signed for a big club!” sing the Brentford fans, in reference to the club almost signing Gray two summers ago. Football fans never forget.

    According to recent reports, another Brentford goal would put them top of the table, for what that is worth. Spurs enjoying some possession in the Brentford half now, but it is entirely sterile.

    It has been revealed that igor Thiago’s shot is blocked, Brentford still look the more likely team to score the next goal. Jadon Anthony shows he has a long throw, which might be a small reason why Brentford decided to sign him. Janelt then drags back Maddison.

    It has been revealed that jadon Anthony involved in some Brenford pressure that results in a long throw and a corner, but the new man then slices a volley over the bar. Standing ovation at the Gtech for Sangare as he makes way for Damsgaard, while Hickey replaces Kayode. Be tough to beat his performance as debut of the weekend.

    In a recent development, michael Oliver letting some meaty challenges go, the game is quite feisty despite the scoreline. Schade rolled out himself into a tackle on Solanke but he did not really catch him with his studs.

    According to recent reports, A few Spurs fans may have thought better of staying to watch the final 20 minutes. I wonder “if” this Spurs fan has switched the television off?

    First match if season . Smiling before the game. Hope to be smiling after. pic.twitter.com/hsTc79PBti.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The New York Mets and center fielder A.J. Ewing have agreed to an eight-year contract extension, SNY reports. The deal will pay Ewing a guaranteed $95 million and includes an option for a ninth year, according to The Athletic. The extension will run through the 2034 season and, if the option is exercised, through 2035.

    Ewing, 22, is coming off a 2026 rookie campaign in which he batted .252/.324/.376 (97 OPS+) with 11 home runs and 25 stolen bases in 120 games for the Mets. Additionally, Ewing graded out as a pronounced defensive asset in center field according to the eye test and fielding metrics. His overall WAR of 3.1 this past season helped him crack the top 10 in the National League Rookie of the Year vote.

    Industry observers note that the Mets originally selected Ewing in the fourth round of the 2023 draft out of an Ohio high school. Following a strong campaign at Double-A and Triple-A in 2025, Ewing entered the 2026 season as a consensus top-100 prospect in baseball. In terms of overall value, he's already begun living up to those expectations.

    The extension expresses confidence on the club's side that Ewing will continue to be a valuable core contributor for years to come. Even if the bat doesn't develop as hoped, Ewing's foundation of excellent defense at an up-the-middle position provides him a high floor of worth over the long term. He's part of an emerging core of young Mets talent that also includes starting pitcher Nolan McLean and Ewing's fellow outfielder Carson Benge, who both finished ahead of Ewing in that Rookie of the Year balloting. As well, catcher Francisco Alvarez is still just 25 years old.

    It has been revealed that no matter what happens with the Mets' high ambitions on the free-agent market, Ewing will be an essential part of the Mets' efforts to move beyond the disappointments of 2026. This past season, the Mets finished 14 games below .500 and in last place in the NL East despite having the league's highest Opening Day payroll.

    The uncertain 2026-27 Major League Baseball offseason is fully underway. The ongoing CBA negotiations and the near certainty of an owner-implemented lockout on Dec. 2 loom over all, and it may indeed mean a flurry of trades and free agent signings leading up to that date. That was certainly the case leading up to the last lockout of 2021-22, and this time around we've already seen some leading examples.

    According to recent reports, thanks to that prospect of a hastened pace, offseason rumors are flowing. Speaking of which, we'll be here each day to round up what's out there. You can find Saturday's supply just below.

    It has been revealed that will the San Francisco Giants trade their ace this offseason? That's a reasonable question to ask now that FanSided is reporting that the Giants are open to trade discussions regarding veteran right-hander Logan Webb. No doubt, Webb would be a coveted presence on the offseason market.

    Webb, who just recently turned 30, endured a bit of a down 2026 on the run-prevention front, but the overall body of work remains very strong. For his career, the three-time All-Star has a career ERA+ of 115 with three top-10 finishes in the American League Cy Young vote. In three of the past four seasons, he's topped 200 innings.

    Webb is under contract through 2028, and that extra year of team control makes him even more of an alluring trade target for contenders in need of rotation upgrades.

    Freddy Peralta, who'll be going into his age-31 season in 2027, is one of the strongest free-agent starting pitchers on the market not named Tarik Skubal. As such, there's healthy interest in his services. The Tampa Bay Rays, the Chicago White Sox, the San Diego Padres, the Toronto Blue Jays, and two presently unknown clubs all have significant interest in signing Peralta, the Athletic reports.

    Peralta, coming off three straight seasons for the Milwaukee Brewers in which he topped 30 starts and 200 strikeouts, wasn't himself with the Latest York Mets for the first half-plus of 2027. However, after a deadline trade to the Rays, he made some adjustments and re-established himself as a highly useful starter. The market's going to reflect his rediscovered form.

    Right-hander Hiromi Itoh, who's seeking to make the leap from Japan to MLB, was recently in Chicago to visit the Cubs or the White Sox, ESPN reports. Both Windy City squads are in need of pitching help, and Itoh would certainly help them on that front.

    The 29-year-old Itoh ranked 26th on CBS Sports' offseason list of the top free agents in the current class. Here's part of our write-up:.

    "A down 2026 season took some of the shine off Itoh, who won the 2025 Eiji Sawamura Award (Japan's Cy Young equivalent) after throwing 196 ⅔ innings with a 2.52 ERA. To be sure, Itoh pitched well in 2026 (3.18 ERA in 172 ⅔ innings), but he was not as consistently dominant as in the past. The 5-foot-9 right-hander is a seven-pitch pitcher with a low-90s fastball and the usual array of secondary pitches (sinker, cutter, curveball, slider, sweeper, splitter), none of which stands out as a plus offering. Itoh has thrown at least 150 innings in each of the last six seasons. He's seen as a crafty back-end starter in MLB, or perhaps even a reliever (Itoh sat 96 mph out of the bullpen in the World Baseball Classic). The Hokkaido Nippon Ham Fighters are expected to post Itoh, who turned 29 in August, this winter.".

    The Cubs have a lot of uncertainty in the rotation, while the White Sox still need help even after adding Dustin May this offseason.

    The New York Mets retained the services of first baseman Mark Vientos leading up to the recent non-tender deadline despite his pattern of decline over the last two seasons. Now, Vientos could be on the move. The soon-to-be 27-year-old has been the subject of trade inquiries, The Athletic reports.

    Recent findings suggest that while Vientos is coming off a highly disappointing 2026 season, he still has power potential and in his semi-recent past a 2024 campaign in which he hit 27 home runs in 111 games. All of that makes Vientos a fairly compelling change-of-scenery possibility, and the Mets may seek to make that happen this winter.

    Former Steelers coach Mike Tomlin on Aaron Rodgers-Mike McCarthy saga: 'It's a dumpster fire'

    📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1336 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • The Pittsburgh Steelers are facing a unique kind of adversity as they prepare for their "Black Friday" matchup against the Denver Broncos.
    • It has been revealed that rodgers' attack of his head coach felt personal and unprecedented.
    • Recent findings suggest that fans and former players have not been shy in voicing their opinions on this wild saga, but one man we all wanted to hear from about this situation was Mike Tomlin.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The Pittsburgh Steelers are facing a unique kind of adversity as they prepare for their "Black Friday" matchup against the Denver Broncos. Late Tuesday night, the team confirmed it was benching future Hall of Fame quarterback Aaron Rodgers in favor of Mason Rudolph. On Wednesday, Rodgers appeared on "The Pat McAfee Show" and lashed out against Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy. That led to his release.

    It has been revealed that rodgers' attack of his head coach felt personal and unprecedented. On national television, he accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings, not putting in the work required to prepare for upcoming opponents, and failing to connect with players in his first season as the lead man in Pittsburgh. The breaking point, according to Rodgers, was when McCarthy, 63, broke down the team saying, "1-2-3 Packers!" at halftime of Sunday's loss to the Philadelphia Eagles. McCarthy last coached the Packers in 2018. The coach admitted using the wrong team name during a press conference on Wednesday.

    Recent findings suggest that fans and former players have not been shy in voicing their opinions on this wild saga, but one man we all wanted to hear from about this situation was Mike Tomlin. The new NBC analyst spent 19 years as the head coach of the Steelers, winning Super Bowl XLIII with the franchise in 2009. He famously never registered a losing season with the Steelers, and coached Rodgers during his final year as coach in 2025. During halftime of the Kansas City Chiefs at Buffalo Bills matchup on Thanksgiving, he revealed what he thought about Rodgers' actions in an interview with Mike Tirico.

    Tomlin said he had a range of emotions hearing what Rodgers had to say about his newly introduced head coach, but the prevailing emotion was "general sadness.".

    "Sad that we might be looking at the end of a legendary career in the quarterback Aaron Rodgers, and just at the macro level whether it's organizationally or for the game of football at large, to see laundry aired out that way in a public forum," Tomlin noted. "Those are things that kind of run counterculture to professional football.".

    Did it shock Tomlin that Rodgers went this route?

    "It certainly did," Tomlin said. "Particularly because I know both men involved. [I] certainly had a lot of intimate work and development of relationships with Aaron over the last couple of years and have known and competed with Mike and respected and appreciated him as a coach for a long time.".

    Tomlin was asked how Rodgers was viewed in the locker room during his one year in Pittsburgh.

    In a recent development, "He was beloved, and I'm not over-exaggerating that," Tomlin said. "He worked at it, and people appreciated his openness to getting to know and understand the Steeler culture. To be engaged with teammates, and particularly from my perspective, I worked with a lot of veteran players over the years and at times they lose a little patience for the process or they lose patience for relationships with younger guys, etcetera. Man, he seemed to embrace all of that and really embrace it in a real natural way.".

    Tomlin was asked whether McCarthy can effectively lead this team for the rest of the season?

    "You know it certainly created some challenges and 'challenges' is probably an understatement if all of those things are true. Certainly, the '1-2-3 Packers' is because he acknowledged that. But his ability to overcome that or inability to overcome that in my opinion is based on relationships, and the depth of those relationships and how those guys feel about him or how those guys buy into what he's selling. And so certainly he's been there a short period of time, and so it makes you wonder the level of that challenge. But it will be relationship-based, his ability to overcome the things that you mentioned.".

    Tirico asked Tomlin what his emotions were being a coach that was involved with the Steelers franchise for nearly two decades.

    "I'm upset about it, it's a dumpster fire," Tomlin said. "And I don't say that in a judgemental way; I've presided over a few dumpster fires in my 19 years. But it certainly is upsetting, and I'm sure Steeler Nation is upset.".

    According to recent reports, there were plenty of bewildering aspects of this story. Tom Pelissero reported that frustration had been building behind the scenes among some players and coaches about Rodgers, who was calling plays himself. The quarterback reportedly went to McCarthy and demanded more changes related to the play-calling process. The coach received feedback from players and coaches indicating that's not what they wanted. Rodgers then issued an ultimatum: "Run things my way, or I quit.".

    In a recent development, ESPN's Brooke Pryor also reported that "multiple league sources corroborated Rodgers' account" during his appearance on ESPN. According to Pryor, "One source texted: 'It's all true.'" Anonymous team sources acknowledged Rodgers' claim that McCarthy fell asleep in meetings, according to The Athletic.

    With that said, Rodgers did violate "the sanctity of the NFL locker room," as Tom Brady mentioned during his broadcast of the Thanksgiving matchup between the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys. One of the best quarterbacks in NFL history dropped a grenade in his building and walked away.

    “Nobody wins when the family feuds.”@TomBrady on Aaron Rodgers pic.twitter.com/qLtmKL5oif.

    The Steelers locker room was expectedly mum on the situation, but quarterback Drew Allar did say it was "kinda sad to see," because of the respect he has for Rodgers.

    According to recent reports, there were plenty of others that did not hold their tongues, however. Former Packers offensive lineman T.J. Lang alleged Rodgers was a hypocrite for blacklisting players for telling the truth at other times, then going scorched-earth this week. Lang even said he's in a group chat with "a whole lot of former teammates" that feel the exact same way that he does.

    "I think it's despicable," Lang remarked on 97.1 The Ticket in Detroit. "I think that Aaron Rodgers just became everything that he has bitched about and moaned about over the last 10 years with former coaches, former teammates airing grievances out, giving opinions out in the media. He has blacklisted, I don't know how many former teammates from just simple comments telling the truth because he just he was sick of it.".

    TJ Lang on his former teammate Aaron Rodgers pic.twitter.com/0oiS3PybCn.

    Former Packers receiver and teammate James Jones stated something very similar.

    "How do you jump on Pat McAfee's show and say all this? Come on, man," Jones noted on the Speakeasy podcast. "My text thread is full of texts and group chats with a lot of my teammates right now, and none are on 12's side, especially the ones that know Mike.".

    Another former Packers wideout in Greg Jennings chimed in on "First Things First," saying he was surprised by a lot of Rodgers' comments, and called his decision to air out this dirty laundry "distasteful.".

    Recent findings suggest that "If you truly cared about more than just yourself, then you don't do this to everybody in that locker room that you just called brothers," Jennings stated. "They are playing for something. You are no longer playing for anything.".

    In a recent development, @GregJennings weighs in on Steelers releasing former teammate Aaron Rodgers:“It was very distasteful… If you truly cared about more than just yourself, then you don’t do this to everybody in that locker room that you just called brothers... They are playing for something.” pic.twitter.com/whPyBO7K2p.

    Steelers president Art Rooney II released a statement on Thursday saying he stands behind McCarthy despite Rodgers' criticisms.

    Sources indicate that "I just want to say that I have 100% confidence in Mike McCarthy and I expect he'll be our coach this season, next season and beyond," Rooney told the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette. "The big thing, what happened this week, is insubordination can't be tolerated in any organization. When you start getting ultimatums, you can't live with that.".

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, coming off a disaster of a season and with a roster badly in need of an overhaul, the Giants make sense as a team to make a trade or two this offseason.
    • Webb, 30, has two years and $47 million left on his current deal.
    • It has been revealed that which teams might make for a good fit for Webb?
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, coming off a disaster of a season and with a roster badly in need of an overhaul, the Giants make sense as a team to make a trade or two this offseason. Sure enough, they are "listening to trade offers" for All-Star starting pitcher Logan Webb, per The Athletic, but they'd need a "very strong return" in order to deal him.

    Webb, 30, has two years and $47 million left on his current deal. He went 8-9 with a 4.31 ERA and 1.3 WAR last season, but it was his worst year in quite a while. He averaged 4.5 WAR per season in the previous four years with a 3.22 ERA and led the National League in innings pitched from 2023 to 2025, racking up three straight top-six Cy Young finishes.

    It has been revealed that which teams might make for a good fit for Webb? Many of them. We're talking about a workhorse under team control for two more years. Let's run through five of the best fits while, again, knowing that basically any contender should be interested in at least a conversation with the Giants.

    Industry observers note that the Cubs need so much pitching this offseason. Their entire rotation heading into the playoffs last season is in free agency. This isn't hyperbole. Matthew Boyd, Shota Imanaga, Kevin Gausman, Clay Holmes and David Peterson are all off the roster. If the Cubs were to try and put together a rotation right now, it would be something like Justin Steele, Edward Cabrera, Javier Assad and several question marks. Ben Brown and Cade Horton will open the season on the injured list.

    Sources indicate that do we really need to spell out what a reliable innings eater would mean for this bunch? Webb is an outstanding fit here.

    Sources indicate that the upstart playoff team last season was a ton of fun, but also was running bullpen games in the ALDS. The White Sox just attached Davis Martin to Luis Castillo in a trade to the Rockies in order to offload Castillo's contract, too, so they're down a starter. The Dustin May signing means they have him along with Sean Burke and converted reliever Grant Taylor. The White Sox would reportedly like to sign another starter in the May ballpark, but what about trading for someone better like Webb?

    A top four in the rotation of Webb, Burke, Taylor and May would be exponentially better than what the Sox had last season.

    It has been revealed that returns of Spencer Strider and Spencer Schwellenbach at some point will help, but this is still a thin rotation for a team coming off a division title. Chris Sale remains, but he's followed up with Grant Holmes and Bryce Elder before the Spencers return. Youngster Didier Fuentes moving to the rotation is exciting, but there are an awful lot of questions behind Sale, who turns 38 in late March, by the way.

    Given that the Padres reside in the NL West with the Giants, there might be a bit of an intradivision tax in terms of the asking price, but Padres boss A.J. Preller is never shy about offloading prospects. There could certainly be a fit. The Padres need rotation help, too, after losing Michael King, Nick Pivetta, Robbie Ray and others to free agency. We know they're in on Tarik Skubal, but that doesn't mean they'll be content with just landing one big fish.

    Look at the current Padres rotation. It's basically Joe Musgrove and Randy Vásquez. With three straight playoff berths and zero trips to the World Series, now isn't the time to have Jhony Brito, Ryan Weiss and Ian Koenig make up 60% of the rotation.

    Dealing for Webb and signing Skubal would make for a nice offseason for upcoming ownership, no?

    In a recent development, one of the most disappointing teams in baseball last season needs to have a prolific offseason. We've heard plenty about the Mets being involved in the Skubal sweepstakes and we've seen them win a monster bidding war before (see: Soto, Juan). Grabbing Webb would make it quite a well-rounded rotation with talented youngsters Nolan McLean, Christian Scott and Zac Thornton.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, welcome to the most special week in the NFL. We watched the Los Angeles Rams defeat the Green Bay Packers on Wednesday night, and now, we have three exciting Thanksgiving matchups to digest this "Turkey Day.".

    Industry observers note that football fans suffered through many sleepy Chicago Bears vs. Detroit Lions Thanksgiving matchups over the years. Now, this 1 p.m. game on Thursday is expected to be one of the most exciting holiday matchups in recent memory. After that, the Dallas Cowboys will welcome Joe Milton III and the Philadelphia Eagles to AT&T Stadium. Both teams are coming off wins, and the Cowboys need this game if they want to keep pace in the NFC East. At the end of the night, we have a potential AFC Championship preview to watch when the Buffalo Bills host Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs. This is just the second game in NFL history to feature two teams coming off at least three straight 17-point victories.

    Which teams should you pick in Week 12, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 25 over at DraftKings Sportsbook.

    Sources indicate that dajani (Broncos -3.5): Aaron Rodgers lobbed a grenade into the Pittsburgh Steelers facility as he exited it this week. Going on national television and calling your coach a narcoleptic, unhealthy, lazy person who doesn't even know the franchise he works for is insane. So, this is a moment that will ultimately rally the locker room, or cause them to completely fall apart. Pick which side you'd like. The Steelers have also won and covered in six straight home games. This seems like an appropriate time for that streak to end   …  Prediction: Broncos 20, Steelers 13.

    Sources indicate that dubin (Broncos -3.5): After the disaster that hit the Steelers this week, I just can't see them keeping the game close against the Broncos. No, I don't think they'll get the backup quarterback bounce from Mason Rudolph. I don't trust the Broncos as far as Bo Nix or I can throw them, but given the state the Steelers' locker room has to be in right now, I think you have to roll with Denver to cover this one with relative ease. … Prediction: Broncos 24, Steelers 10.

    Dajani (Ravens +7): I have the Houston Texans winning this game, but seven points seems a bit high. C.J. Stroud is playing some great football, but his production has been overshadowed by a defense that has fallen from No. 2 in points allowed per game in 2025, to 17th this year. The Texans are 1-8 against the spread in their last nine home games following an ATS win. I'll take Baltimore to keep it close… Prediction: Texans 24, Ravens 18.

    Industry observers note that dubin (Ravens +7): The Ravens have now lost six straight, but they've lost the two games in the Jacoby Brissett era by a combined five points despite turning the ball over six times in those contests.     📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Welcome to Thanksgiving week. Here in Major League Baseball news, that normally means we're bound for a slow week -- save for a few notable exceptions -- but with the CBA expiring on Dec. 1, we might just be in for a free agent frenzy. Let's hope that's the case.

    We can start today's set of news and rumors with the biggest free agent out there.

    Tarik Skubal is the No. 1 free agent this offseason and the two-time Cy Young winner appears on pace to make a decision before the CBA expires. Skubal's agent, Scott Boras, hit MLB Network Radio on Sunday and said that there's a "strong likelihood" that a decision comes by that Dec. 1 deadline, especially given that Skubal's signing impacts so many other pitchers (Boras mentioned that it impacts "10-15 pitchers").

    The 30-year-old lefty was 12-7 with a 2.72 ERA and 186 strikeouts in 158 ⅔ innings last season, as he bounced back after just six weeks from elbow surgery.

    The teams most heavily involved in the Skubal rumors to this point have been the Dodgers, Mets, Padres and Blue Jays, all of whom had in-person meetings with him last week.

    The Tigers have agreed to a deal with right-hander Luis Gil, per ESPN. It's a one-year, $2.3 million deal.

    According to recent reports, gil won the American League Rookie of the Year after a productive 2024 season in which he won 15 games and had a 3.50 ERA, but he spent a good portion of 2026 in the minors and was nontendered by the Yankees on Friday. In his limited MLB time last season, Gil had a 4.61 ERA, 1.43 WHIP and 17 strikeouts in 27 ⅓ innings.

    The Tigers rotation seems set with Framber Valdez, Troy Melton, Keider Montero, Jackson Jobe and River Ryan, so consider Gil a depth option.

    The Red Sox also reportedly highlighted interest.

    #153694. Kyrie Irving to the Jazz? Why Utah's reported interest in the star Mavericks guard makes no sense

    📅 19 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1423 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

    Kyrie Irving to the Jazz? Why Utah's reported interest in the star Mavericks guard makes no sense

    📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1423 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

    ⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • They will consider almost any path to improving their rosters, no matter how obscure or unexpected.
    • On Thursday, one such rumor arrived as SNY's Ian Begley reported that the Utah Jazz have given Kyrie Irving "internal consideration as a potential trade candidate." Now, this is common.
    • So, let's consider this rumor in earnest.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    NBA teams are remarkably diligent. They will consider almost any path to improving their rosters, no matter how obscure or unexpected. Still, every now and then, a truly bizarre nugget hits the rumor mill and forces us to consider what exactly a team is thinking.

    On Thursday, one such rumor arrived as SNY's Ian Begley reported that the Utah Jazz have given Kyrie Irving "internal consideration as a potential trade candidate." Now, this is common. Teams will do due diligence on a wide variety of players leading up to transaction periods in order to make sure they've covered their bases, and Begley gives no indication that there have even been talks between the Jazz and the Dallas Mavericks. Still, as he notes, "you're not gonna spend a lot of time on a player if you don't have any interest in him, so the idea of Utah spending some time internally on Kyrie Irving was interesting.".

    So, let's consider this rumor in earnest. The Jazz entered this season with playoff expectations after four straight years in the lottery. They are 3-13 due to a combination of injuries, players adjusting to a new roster and simply poor performance. Utah has shown a willingness to trade for players outside of its perceived timeline before. The Jazz looked at then-33-year-old Jrue Holiday early in their rebuild in 2023, for instance, but backed off when Holiday's camp reportedly made it clear he would not be interested in extending.

    Irving, still a star-caliber scorer, has the Mavericks at 8-7 through 15 games. He's averaging over 22 points on roughly his standard efficiency for a Dallas team with pretty limited shooting around him. We can't say at this stage whether or not the Mavericks are willing to trade him. The notion that they might depends on the team's asset deficit (Dallas does not control its own first-round pick again until 2031) and the 15-year age gap between Irving and franchise player Cooper Flagg, but Dallas could easily elect to simply build off this early success.

    According to recent reports, if they do take the long view and consider trade offers, Irving could absolutely help a team trying to win right now. Plenty of teams potentially looking for individual shot-creation, like the Detroit Pistons, Houston Rockets and Miami Heat, could be planning pursuits of the future Hall of Famer.

    The question here is why the Jazz, specifically, would be interested in Irving, because on paper, there is perhaps not a single, high-profile player who makes less sense for this roster than he does. Utah's young core revolves around three perimeter players: Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson and Ace Bailey. The Jazz are so strong on that front that Bailey came off the bench to start the season, and it's unclear how exactly they initiative to handle their starting five when Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. return from injuries. If Utah isn't comfortable with Jackson playing center full time, and the Memphis Grizzlies certainly weren't, then one of those five players either needs to get traded or come off the bench.

    Adding Irving to this logjam doesn't make sense. Neither does trading one of those players for Irving. George is 23. Bailey is 20. Peterson is 19. Teams that are 10 games below .500 simply don't trade foundational pieces for players a decade or more their senior. They gave up three first-round picks for Jackson largely to improve their defense, and now that Walker Kessler plays for the Los Angeles Lakers, his presence matters more than ever.

    Recent findings suggest that markkanen is the obvious trade candidate of the group, but he's still five years younger than Irving and plays a less saturated position. If Utah viewed Markkanen's max contract as a negative it needed to escape, that would be one thing, but there's just no evidence at this stage that this is the case. They have rebuffed trade interest in Markkanen at every turn. If Dallas were willing to put substantial draft equity on the table to cover the age and positional gaps here, there could perhaps be a conversation, but Dallas isn't in a position to do so.

    According to recent reports, there's some merit to the idea that Utah might eventually want to shake up its backcourt. There were rumors during the draft process that Peterson's representatives were skeptical of Utah as a landing spot because they also represent George and felt that two score-first guards would clash. Even if the Jazz were prepared to split them up less than 20 games into Peterson's career, Irving himself has typically fared far better when he has been paired with a high-level passer. He won his championship with LeBron James. He's thriving next to Cooper Flagg now. His best trait is, and always has been, his scoring.

    And then, of course, there is the history shared between Irving and Utah's top executive. The CEO of the Jazz is Danny Ainge, who once traded for Irving when he ran the Boston Celtics. Before his second season in Boston, Irving publicly shared plans to re-sign with the Celtics as a free agent in 2019. When the time came, he instead joined the Brooklyn Nets, a divisional opponent. This is the NBA. If LeBron James can reunite with Dan Gilbert, any player-executive reunion is theoretically possible. Nonetheless, Ainge and Irving would seemingly be among the unlikeliest pairings in all of basketball. Put all of this together and this is a puzzling rumor to say the least.

    Sometimes a rumor indicates more about a team's significant-picture plans than it does a specific target. For a variety of reasons, some of which we've covered, it seems exceedingly unlikely that the Jazz are going to trade for Irving. However, they've invested the time in considering it, as Begley noted. That means something, even if it doesn't mean a trade is coming.

    In a recent development, the simplest read on this is that Utah is concerned enough about its short-term prospects that it is considering investing in win-now help despite its 3-13 start. That, in itself, makes sense. The Jazz don't control their own first-round pick this season. They have no incentive to lose, and while making the postseason despite starting the season 10 games under .500 is improbable, it just happened a year ago when the 4-14 Charlotte Hornets recovered promptly enough to reach the Play-In Tournament. The Jazz are 5.5 games out of the No. 10 seed in the Western Conference right now. If they get healthy in time and make the right addition, perhaps they could still make a real run at it.

    Skepticism about the George-Peterson fit, for now, should be on the back burner. Though the two fared far better early on when they played separately, both, at least for now, have better net ratings and true shooting percentages in the minutes they've shared than the minutes they haven't. George's usage skyrockets when he plays without Peterson, but that's to be expected with Markkanen and Jackson out.

    In a recent development, there may have been concern early in the season, and that might have been when Irving crossed Utah's mind. There may still be concerns down the line when the Jazz have had a longer sample size to evaluate the pairing with the rest of their roster. For now, though, it's simply too early to consider splitting up such a talented tandem, especially right as the team has actually started winning some games.

    However, ball-handling behind them is a valid concern. Utah declined its fourth-year option on backup point guard and former first-round pick Isaiah Collier, and the offense has been 6.5 points per 100 possessions worse with him on the floor this season. Adding a veteran backup point guard, if only to ease Peterson's burden during the minutes George rests, would be sensible. Irving is obviously no backup, but as perhaps the most notable point guard theoretically on the market, it makes sense that the Jazz would at least broach the concept internally.

    In a recent development, ainge hasn't earned the nickname "Trader Danny" for nothing. His teams are almost always at the center of the trade market, and as last year's Jackson deal proved, he's as capable of a stunner as he's ever been. Irving would certainly qualify as one. We shouldn't expect it. It wouldn't really make sense based on what we know now. But in the post-Luka Dončić trade NBA, it would be hard to dismiss basically any rumor involving a player of this stature.

    • According to recent reports, that's three consecutive winning weeks for me, which is a major positive.
    • I can see .500 now after being buried under it at the start of the season.
    • Sources indicate that this is Thanksgiving Week, which is usually a good week for me.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, that's three consecutive winning weeks for me, which is a major positive. I was 7-6 against the spread last week and 9-4 straight up. My straight-up record is now 104-58-1, while my ATS record is 75-85-3.

    I can see .500 now after being buried under it at the start of the season.

    Sources indicate that this is Thanksgiving Week, which is usually a good week for me. And I feel good about the picks.

    Recent findings suggest that it starts Wednesday night with a good one between the Packers and Rams, and it ends Monday night with the Bucs against the Panthers. I really like the teams in both of those games.

    It has been revealed that we have NFL games Wednesday, Thursday (Thanksgiving), Friday, Sunday and Monday. What a feast.

    I know I will as the climb to .500 ATS continues.

    All lines via DraftKings; All times ET.

    Recent findings suggest that this Friday game pits two teams who would be in the playoffs right now. But the Steelers have lost two straight and haven't looked good. Denver has won six in a row. But I think the Steelers will find a way to show up and win this one behind their running game. It won't be pretty, but the Steelers will find a way.

    The Bengals are coming off a tough road loss at Washington, while the Saints are playing consecutive road games. The Bengals offense didn't score as it had in Monday's game, but that will change here. Joe Burrow gets back on track. Bengals massive.

    Recent findings suggest that the Giants are coming off an impressive victory over the Jaguars, while the Colts are coming off a bye. They released quarterback Daniel Jones, which means Anthony Richardson will be starting. The Giants' defense should dominate in this one. The Colts have packed it in, so the Giants take it.

    Recent findings suggest that the Jets are playing consecutive road games, while the Dolphins are home for the first time in three weeks. The Jets played well in beating the Chargers last week, while Miami lost to the Bills. The Dolphins are limited on offense, but the Jets' defense has struggled. Look for Miami to hang around.

    The Vikings are home after getting blown out by the 49ers in Mexico. The Falcons are off a bye. The Minnesota offense struggled against the 49ers, but the Falcons have had defensive problems lately. Look for the Minnesota defense to get back on track as well. Vikings take it.

    The Jaguars are coming off a bad showing in the loss to the Giants, while Tennessee gave up 51 to the Cowboys last week. Ouch. The Jaguars scored 40 against them two weeks ago. They won't get that many here, but it will still be ugly as Trevor Lawrence and the passing game get back on track.

    Industry observers note that this is essentially a playoff game of sorts for these two. The loser is pretty much done. The Texans are home off a Thursday game, while the Ravens are playing consecutive road games. Edge Houston. The Texans have played well on offense, and the Ravens' defense is a mess. Look for a big day for C.J. Stroud.

    Sources indicate that this was once scheduled for prime time, but it was moved because both teams have flopped this year. The Patriots will start Tommy DeVito for the injured Drake Maye. That's a problem. The Chargers might not have Justin Herbert (concussion) either, which would put D.J. Uiagalelei in as the starter. He's thrown seven passes in his career. Even so, give me the home team here.

    The Commanders are coming off an impressive home victory Monday night over the Bengals, while the Cardinals got rocked by the Chiefs last week. Arizona has major-time complications and fired the defensive coordinator this week. That defense will struggle to stop Jayden Daniels. The Commanders stay hot.

    Pick: Commanders 30, Cardinals 19.

    Industry observers note that the 49ers have the best record in the NFC and seem to be cruising to the division title. But Seattle can slow that talk down here with a victory. That will be tough to do on the road. Look for a lower-scoring game in the second division game between the two — the 49ers won the first — and San Francisco will win it late.

    Recent findings suggest that this has been flexed to prime time because the Browns would be a playoff team right now. Plus, the Raiders have rookie Fernando Mendoza making his third start. The Raiders are playing consecutive road games, and Cleveland is off a bye. Big edge to the Browns as they win it behind their defense.

    The Panthers can take a stronghold on the division with a victory here. They come in with defensive concerns, but the Bucs have problems in the passing game. So what gives? I think the Tampa Bay defense will play well here and the Bucs will run it right at Carolina to win it like they did in the first meeting.

    Dak Prescott has thrown nine touchdown passes and no picks in the past two weeks. The Dallas offense is rolling. The Eagles defense will be a challenge. Joe Milton, who was on the Cowboys' practice squad, will start at quarterback for the Eagles. Dallas will play better defense against him this week. Cowboys big.

    This is the game of the week. Patrick Mahomes vs. Josh Allen. What's not to like as two of the best in the league go at it? The Bills have played much better defense lately, but they've faced a bunch of backup quarterbacks. Not here. So look for both passers to have good days. In the end, Allen will make the significant play late to win it.

    Industry observers note that this should be an offensive show. Both teams can score, even if Chicago hasn't been great on offense the past two games. On this fast track, look out. The Bears defense has played well since getting Jeffrey Simmons in a trade, but they won't stop the Lions here. Look for a lot of points with the home team getting the victory on Thanksgiving.

    The Packers get Micah Parsons back, while the Rams will be without Puka Nacua for the rest of the season. Their offense is limited without him. But this game will be decided by how well the Packers' line can block Aaron Donald and Myles Garrett. They've been bad, but I think they will be better here. The defense will keep this close, and Jordan Love will win it late.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    The NBA season started one month ago today. The first stanza of the campaign brought a great deal of excitement at the top of the league with superstars doing superstar things and most of the projected championship contenders getting off to hot starts. But we also saw injuries, a disappointing first handful of games from Mikal Bridges and an Eastern Conference that is not nearly as dominant as it was supposed to be.

    Those are three of the biggest letdowns of the young season. Here's our John Gonzalez on why Bridges might be the greatest dud of any individual player:.

    According to recent reports, another major disappointment: The Kings. How can a team underperform expectations when those expectations are already about as low as they come? Well, Sacramento sure has found a way. With a 1-13 record and after a puzzling trade, the Kings earned their spot in our ranking of the NBA's most hopeless teams.

    In a recent development, the College Football Selection Committee is in love with the SEC. Only one time in three different rankings have the bracket-makers ranked a team from that conference lower than AP Top 25 voters. Whether or not you think it's fair, the numbers largely back it up. In fact, two-loss No. 5 Texas even has a better resume score than undefeated No. 2 Utah! So maybe the committee is not all that out of line. You can be sure they will have their eyes on these five key matchups in Week 12.

    Recent findings suggest that another important clash is the only top-25 contest of the week: No. 1 Georgia at No. 21 South Carolina. In his Six Pack of picks, our Tom Fornelli explained why the Bulldogs will roll on the road.

    Industry observers note that moving away from the SEC, look out for a potential upset in the Substantial Ten. Nothing is going well for Michigan, but the Wolverines are only small underdogs against unbeaten No. 4 UCLA. These five factors will determine whether the Bruins move one step closer to the CFP or fall for the first time this season.

    Here's how to watch the biggest games of Week 12 and our picks for each of them:.

    This is easily the most lopsided week of the NFL season. The Bills and Chiefs are three-score favorites. The Bears and Broncos are also favored by double digits. The Cowboys, Lions, Jaguars and Bengals are all favored by about a touchdown. You know how these things go, though. One of these favorites is bound to lose. We put a few of them on upset alert, and a handful of our experts are in agreement that the Lions are among the most vulnerable.

    Industry observers note that first of all, the Buccaneers have just as much to play for as the Lions. Both of them are locked into tightly contested division battles. The motivation will be there for a Tampa Bay team that could somehow sneak into the playoffs even with a losing record. And then there's the Tampa Bay defense, which has forced at least four turnovers in each of its last three games. Our Tyler Sullivan stated it would not surprise him if Jared Goff's interception streak continues.

    And even though our Jordan Dajani could not bring himself to pick the upset outright, he does see the Buccaneers keeping this one highly competitive.

    Erling Haaland cuts off his trademark blond hair

    📅 23 Aug 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (521 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic latest look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.
    • The Manchester City striker revealed his new buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.
    • Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Erling Haaland has unveiled a dramatic latest look after cutting off his trademark blond locks.

    The Manchester City striker revealed his new buzzcut hairstyle on Sunday morning ahead of his side’s Premier League opener at home to Bournemouth later in the day.

    Later in the episode, Haaland called a host of famous faces, including Oasis singer Noel Gallagher and former City manager Pep Guardiola, to get their opinions on his transformation.

    Pep Guardiola's reaction to Erling Haaland's new haircut. 😭😂📲 Watch: https://t.co/4KvxC9e5mx pic.twitter.com/QQBCKKpGkP.

    Haaland, 26, has not sported short hair since his time at Borussia Dortmund, where he played three seasons before joining City in 2022.

    Sources indicate that haaland removed his hairband during a 4-1 win over Arsenal in 2023 on a raucous night at the Etihad as City beat their title rivals to move one step closer to winning the league. There will be no need for one now, though, with a close-cut look to mark a newly introduced campaign.

    It is a new-look City in more ways than one this term with head coach Enzo Maresca looking to kickstart a new era following Pep Guardiola’s exit.

    Maresca is hoping for an immediate return to form in City’s Premier League opener after a chastening 3-0 defeat by Arsenal in the Community Shield last week.

    So far, only Elliot Anderson has arrived but Maresca is hopeful the club will be active in the transfer market. Rodri has left for Barcelona while Savinho is closing in on a move to Tottenham.

    Industry observers note that “I’ll try to find a newly introduced Rodri – it is what it is,” the former Chelsea manager remarked. “Rodri, before he arrived here, he didn’t win the Ballon d’Or, he didn’t win the Champions League, he didn’t win the Club World Cup.     Industry observers note that “When they leave, you need to be good and recruit the next one. They are all similar – David, Kevin, Fernandinho, Rodri, Agüero, Erling. It’s just normal, it’s a change. It’s not a problem, just go again and try to do the right things.”.

    You're probably on your second or third nap by now, right? No, we're not saying you're Mike McCarthy, nor are we saying you could coach the Pittsburgh Steelers (or Green Bay Packers, for that matter). We're merely pointing out that you've consumed enough tryptophan from the Thanksgiving turkey that you're probably a little lethargic. And if that means you dozed off during some of the NFL's Thanksgiving triple-header, that's alright. We're here to help you sift through what went down over the holiday slate and make you sound smart.

    According to recent reports, given that all three games were in individual windows and the entire nation was huddled around the table to watch them, there will be a lot of opinions that spew out of them. Some will be justified, while others you'll rightfully tilt your head, squint your eyebrows, and judge silently. We'll make you the former.

    Below, we'll go through some of the top storylines from each Thanksgiving game and determine if they're something to take seriously or if they're merely overreactions.

    Overreaction vs. reality: Overreaction.

    Industry observers note that when it comes to statement wins, you won't find many bigger than the Bears rolling into Ford Field and pulling off the 39-35 win over the Lions. Chicago scored the game-winning touchdown with just three seconds left in regulation and erased an 11-point fourth-quarter deficit. That victory puts the Bears at 9-2 on the season, and that has them atop the NFC North.

    THAT'S A TOUCHDOWN!!!!!!📺: CBS pic.twitter.com/IOUvYvWOHa.

    According to recent reports, naturally, confidence is sky-high that Chicago will eventually secure the division title for the second straight year, and rightfully so. How can you not feel that way after such a marquee win? Should they be printing the hats and T-shirts, however? That's a different discussion entirely.

    While Chicago owns the inside track, the NFC North is far from being solidified. The Bears still have three division matchups on the docket over their final six games of the season. Outside of facing NFC North rivals, they'll also square off against the Jaguars and Bills. The only sure-fire victory is when they visit the Miami Dolphins in Week 14. With the margins still razor-thin, and the Bears at the moment 1-2 in the division, they are not on as solid ground as this latest win would suggest.

    Overreaction vs. reality: Overreaction.

    Industry observers note that at the end of the day, the MVP is a quarterback's award. You may not like it, but that's the reality. Gibbs has been otherworldly this season and just put together a historic performance on Thanksgiving. He logged 21 carries for 205 yards, three touchdowns, and five receptions for 47 yards. Those are the second-most rushing yards on Thanksgiving in NFL history, and Gibbs tied Barry Sanders (1997) for the most rushing touchdowns on Thanksgiving by a Lions player in franchise history.

    Gibbs has joined Eric Dickerson (1983) and Priest Holmes (2002) as the only players with at least 1,700 scrimmage yards and 18 total touchdowns in the first 11 games of a season in NFL history.

    JAHMYR GIBBS 70-YARD TOUCHDOWN 🔥 pic.twitter.com/w7oihVzrsd.

    Again, these numbers are bonkers and will almost certainly give Gibbs the inside track at the Offensive Player of the Year award. Those who Jim Nantz pointed out were chanting "MVP" at Ford Field on Thursday, however, will be disappointed. That'll go to Joe Burrow, Brock Purdy, or whichever quarterback endears himself to the NFL at large.

    He may deserve it, but the hardware Gibbs will be eyed for is OPOY and not MVP.

    Industry observers note that overreaction vs. reality: Reality.

    According to recent reports, jalen Hurts is the obvious top option at quarterback once he returns to full health. We're not talking about Hurts' standing as QB1 in Philadelphia. However, Howie Roseman has once again pulled a rabbit out of his hat. He plucked Joe Milton III off Dallas' practice squad, and you can't deny that what we've seen out of Milton doesn't warrant a longer look as a full-time starter in the NFL.

    JOE MILTON AND DEVONTA SMITH DO IT AGAINPHIvsDAL on FOX/FOX One/TubiStream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/hjaMzRC3ub.

    It might not be with the Eagles, but you can't deny the raw ability that Milton possesses. The arm talent is obvious, and he was able to hang in against Dallas in a high-profile Thanksgiving matchup on the road in just his third career start.

    The Eagles have done a fantastic job at parlaying assets into future draft capital. It's not out of the realm of possibility that they do the same with Milton -- who'll be a restricted free agent -- this offseason. For a team searching for a long-term starter at quarterback, why wouldn't you roll the dice on someone like Milton, who is 26 years old? He has far higher upside than Kirk Cousins, Geno Smith, Kyler Murray, and Daniel Jones, who'll also be free agents (albeit unrestricted) this offseason.

    Overreaction vs. reality: Reality.

    Nail, meet coffin. The Cowboys can put their playoff hopes to bed, unofficially. After blowing a 21-point lead to the Eagles on Thanksgiving, Dallas drops to 5-7 on the season. For the moment, they're in third place in the NFC East, and the path to the playoffs feels nonexistent, even if mathematically there's still a chance.

    INTERCEPTED! EAGLES COMPLETE THE COMEBACK! pic.twitter.com/ymk4TF0H8K.

    Industry observers note that they already are on the wrong side of the tiebreaker with the Giants after losing the season opener. They still have a Week 17 matchup to fully determine if that tiebreaker will be a factor. If not, it'll come down to division record, where Fresh York has the advantage through Week 12 (2-1-1 vs. 2-2).

    More dire for Dallas, the road ahead may make division and head-to-head tiebreakers moot. After falling to the Joe Milton-led Eagles, the Cowboys will now have to endure a three-game stretch of facing the Seahawks in Seattle, the Rams in Los Angeles (after the Week 14 bye), and then the Jacksonville Jaguars before they see the Giants. They'll, in all likelihood, be an underdog in all three of those games. If the oddsmakers are proved right, they're 5-10 before they kick off against the Giants.

    After Thursday's showing, it's hard to have any confidence that they'll persevere and make a legitimate push to a division title.

    It has been revealed that overreaction vs. reality: Overreaction.

    It's not that Buffalo won't eventually land the No. 1 seed in the AFC, but it's hardly secure at this point even after a critical head-to-head win over Kansas City. The Bills are 10-1 on the season, which has them on the inside track for the first-round bye at the moment. However, the upcoming month does present some challenges. After heading up to New England to face a Drake Maye-less Patriots, Buffalo will face the Packers (road), Bears, and Broncos (road). That could result in some losses that open the door for some other contenders in the conference.

    Specifically, that Broncos matchup in Denver looms large on Christmas Day as Sean Payton's team is currently the closest to Buffalo for the top spot in the conference. Again, the Bills are in a great position to be the No. 1 seed, but we've got a long way to go before locking in first-round bye plans.

    Nikita Kucherov trade request: Five potential landing spots for the reigning NHL MVP

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • In a recent development, one of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey.
    • Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era.
    • Recent findings suggest that just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    In a recent development, one of the greatest players in Tampa Bay Lightning history may soon be wearing a different jersey. According to Sportsnet, Nikita Kucherov has told the Lightning he won't sign a contract extension and has requested a trade.

    Kucherov, a two-time Stanley Cup champion and two-time Hart Trophy winner as league MVP, is one of the best players of his era. The 33-year-old just passed the legendary Steven Stamkos for the all-time franchise lead in points and has shown no signs of slowing down.

    Recent findings suggest that just last season, Kucherov posted 44 goals and 86 assists en route to his second Hart Trophy win. His underlying numbers were even better with a five-on-five goal differential of plus-38 and an expected goals share of 57.0 percent. Only a select few players can drive play from the wing like Kucherov, and that makes him a unicorn of sorts.

    Industry observers note that kucherov is in the final year of a contract that pays him $9.5 million per season, and with the salary cap rising rapidly, he's due for a gargantuan raise next summer. It sounds like Kucherov and the Lightning were too far apart on that number, so the superstar winger has shifted his focuse to a change of scenery.

    Recent findings suggest that it's crucial to note that Kucherov has limited trade protection in the form of a 10-team trade list, but that should be more than enough for the Lightning to find a suitable trade partner. With that in mind, let's take a look at five teams that would be ideal fits for Kucherov as he prepares for the next chapter of his illustrious career.

    It has been revealed that right out of the gate, this is the most natural fit of all the potential landing spots. General manager Kent Hughes has done a superb job of locking down his young core on team-friendly contracts, and as a result, the Canadiens have nearly $30 million in projected cap space for next season. They also have a glaring need in their top two lines, and I'd say the reigning Hart Trophy winner would fill that role quite nicely.

    Montreal's moment to strike is now. It's an ascendant team with a great salary cap situtation and assets to spend. It's time to make a splash, and this would be a tsunami. Just imagine Kucherov on a power play unit with Nick Suzuki, Cole Caufield, Lane Hutson and Ivan Demidov. Kucherov would also be coached by former Lightning teammate Martin St. Louis, so a rapport would already exist between player and coach. I expect the Canadiens to do everything in their power to land Kucherov.

    Industry observers note that we already know the Wild are big-game hunting at forward because they've been heavily linked to former Detroit Red Wings captain Dylan Larkin. If I were advising general manager Bill Guerin -- and I'm certainly not -- I would recommend Minnesota package whatever assets it has offered Detroit and redirect them to Tampa Bay. No, Kucherov is not a center,  and that's the Wild's biggest need.

    Industry observers note that however, Kucherov is a rare breed of winger in that he can drive play better than most first-line centers from the wing. Put him on a line with Kirill Kaprizov, and the only time opponents will touch the puck is when they're pulling out of the net.

    Recent findings suggest that with Quinn Hughes also on an expiring contract, acquiring Kucherov would be a risky move for the Wild. What if they give up premium assets only to lose Kucherov and Hughes next summer? I don't think fear can dictate Minnesota's decisions. The team has a top-two defenseman in the world on its roster right now, and it has the opportunity to acquire a top-five forward. Worry about next summer when the time comes. Go all in to win the Cup while you have a chance.

    It was no secret that the Hurricanes were in on the Connor Hellebuyck sweepstakes but just missed out. So, if they can't get better at preventing goals, why not get much better at scoring them? Carolina doesn't exactly need any help offensively, but adding Kucherov would go a long way to helping the team repeat as Stanley Cup champions. Besides, Kucherov would provide another level of playmaking and finishing that the Canes don't right now have on their roster.

    Carolina has a good chunk of cap space available already, and it wouldn't need to shed much in order to make room for Kucherov. The Canes also have some enticing young players on their roster that might appeal to the Bolts, and they have three first-round picks over the next two drafts. Why not take a shot at landing a superstar winger?

    Similar to the Hurricanes, the Mammoth were in the mix to acquire Hellebucyk, and for good reason. The goaltending tandem of Karel Vejmelka and Sebastian Cossa has not been good, so Utah may have to outscore its problems until one of the goalies finds a groove. Offense may be the best defense for the Mammoth -- and if that's the case -- then Kucherov should be in the mix for the Norris Trophy. There is a great young core of forwards in Salt Lake City, and I think Kucherov would be a perfect fit alongside Logan Cooley, who is emerging as a franchise center.

    Utah also has plenty of draft capital with which to work, and it's projected for just over $25 million in salary cap space next season. The Mammoth don't have any major pending free agents on their cap sheet, so they're a suitor capable of signing Kucherov to a long-term extension.

    Allow me to get a little bold on the fifth and final destination. The Stars have already failed to sign 27-year-old winger Jason Robertson to a long-term extension once. The two sides agreed to a one-year deal worth $12 million prior to the season, but Robertson's future with the team is still very much in doubt. What if Dallas and Tampa Bay executed a true "hockey trade" -- one player for one player?

    Dallas would get the better player in Kucherov, but there are no guarantees regarding an extension. The Stars are in win-now mode, and Kucherov could help them get over the Cup hump immediately. Tampa Bay would get a younger player in Robertson, and although he doesn't have the elite playmaking ability of Kucherov, he's still an exceptionally talented scorer. Perhaps the Bolts could get him to join the team's core and sign a multi-year contract. This deal could work for both sides.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Ace left-hander Tarik Skubal, winner of the last two American League Cy Young awards and far and away the top free agent of the 2026-27 class, has agreed to terms with the New York Mets on a nine-year contract worth $450 million, reports the New York Post. The deal has a $45 million signing bonus with no options or opt-outs, per SNY, as well as a full no-trade clause, so the Mets have locked Skubal up for the full nine years. Further, there are only $30 million in deferrals, according to the New York Post. The deal is pending a physical.

    Once finalized, the deal will make Skubal the highest-paid pitcher in Major League Baseball history, in terms of both total contract value and average annual salary.

    Skubal, who turned 30 years of age on Nov. 20, is the No. 1 ranked talent on our list of the top 50 free agents for this offseason. Here's part of Mike Axisa's write-up:.

    In a recent development, "Excluding Yoshinobu Yamamoto, who was a special case as a Japanese star with no MLB track record, Skubal is the best starting pitcher to hit free agency since Gerrit Cole in 2019. He highlighted few long-lasting effects from the NanoScope elbow surgery in May and remains a capital-A Ace with terrific surface stats and under-the-hood performance indicators. Skubal brings four swing-and-miss pitches to the table (four-seamer, changeup, slider, curveball), a near MLB-best ability to limit exit velocity, and elite strike-throwing ability (MLB's third-lowest walk rate since 2023). Build an ace starter in a lab and he would look a lot like Skubal. He'll play the entire 2027 season at age 30, and given the things teams can do with pitchers these days, Skubal figures to remain a frontline starter for most of a long-term contract. He's the only true balance-of-power player available in free agency this offseason. Skubal can swing a division race and a postseason series all by himself.".

    Industry observers note that over the last three seasons, Skubal has pitched to a 2.42 ERA and an FIP of 2.48 in 546 innings spread over 88 starts. That amounts to a total WAR of 17.7 since the start of the 2024 campaign. Skubal remains foremost in the discussion for best pitcher in baseball, and this signing reflects that reality.

    Since Skubal was traded to the Los Angeles Dodgers from the Detroit Tigers leading up to the 2026 deadline, he was ineligible to receive the qualifying offer from the Dodgers. As such, the Mets will not be penalized a draft pick for signing Skubal.

    According to recent reports, the nine years here aren't record-setting, as the longest pitcher contract remains the 12-year deal that Yoshinobu Yamamoto signed with the Dodgers. Yamamoto's $325 million was previously the largest contract for a pitcher -- obviously excepting Shohei Ohtani, as he's a two-way player -- so Skubal's $450 million shatters that record.

    Coming off a disappointing 88-loss campaign in 2026, the Mets, big-spending owner Steve Cohen, and lead decision-maker David Stearns needed to make an offseason splash to improve their chances of a 2027 rebound and inspire a perhaps disaffected fan base. Skubal more than qualifies. He'll front a Mets rotation that also includes 25-year-old right-hander Nolan McLean, who himself has frontline long-term potential. In Queens, Skubal joins a roster that also includes the All-Star likes of Juan Soto, Francisco Lindor, and Bo Bichette.

    Further, the Mets just locked up young outfielder A.J. Ewing to an eight-year, $95 million extension and we all know plenty about Soto's monster contract. The Mets now have Soto through 2039, Skubal through 2035, Ewing through 2034 and Lindor through 2031.

    The rotation for the Mets right now looks something like:.

    Recent findings suggest that given the large outlay for Skubal here, the Mets should be all-in on improving the ballclub for the 2027 season, which means we shouldn't expect them to stop with just signing Skubal. That last spot in the rotation, as such, should be ticketed to someone else outside the organization at present, whether a free agent or a trade acquisition.

    The landing of the top free agent available no doubt ramps up the pressure on Stearns and the Mets to deliver a playoff berth and a deep October run in 2027, but Skubal's presence also makes it much likely that such a feat comes to pass.
